question:
(i) Explain why current lags behind voltage in a pure inductive AC circuit.
(ii) How does inductive reactance depend on frequency?
(iii) If the frequency of the AC source is doubled, how will the current through a pure inductor change when the rms voltage and inductance remain constant? Justify your answer.

options.A:
(i) Current leads voltage because an inductor opposes voltage directly.
(ii) $X_L\propto\frac{1}{f}$.
(iii) If frequency doubles, current doubles.
options.B:
(i) Current is in phase with voltage in a pure inductor.
(ii) $X_L$ is independent of frequency.
(iii) If frequency doubles, current is unchanged.
options.C:
(i) In a pure inductor, $v=L\frac{di}{dt}$, so voltage reaches maximum before current; current lags voltage by $\frac{\pi}{2}$.
(ii) $X_L=2\pi fL$, so $X_L\propto f$.
(iii) If frequency doubles, $X_L$ doubles and for fixed rms voltage $I=\frac{V}{X_L}$ becomes half.
options.D:
(i) Current lags voltage by $\pi$.
(ii) $X_L\propto f^2$.
(iii) If frequency doubles, current becomes one-fourth.
